title: Ferrari 296 Challenge Stradale and Challenge Evo Ditch Their Hybrid Systems, Gain Speed

body_markdown:
Ferrari showed off two new versions of its mid-engine, V-6 sports car at Ferrari Finali Mondiali, an end-of-season celebration that also serves as the season finale for the Ferrari Challenge racing series. The 296 Challenge Stradale, stripped of the weight and complexity of its hybrid powertrain, offers “the most direct link to a race car” of any car in its lineup, according to Ferrari. Meanwhile, the 296 Challenge Evo—also operating sans electric-assist—is touted as being “faster, more predictable, and more consistent” when lap times matter.


Ferrari


Ferrari


The 120-degree hot-V engine keeps mass low, and new tuning helps boost low-end torque.


Like the standard 296 coupe and spider, both of the new variants are powered by a twin-turbo, 3.0-liter, 120-degree V-6. In the 296 Challenge Stradale, it’s rated at 670 hp at 8000 rpm, while the 296 Challenge Evo is tuned to develop 700 hp at 7500 rpm. The street-going car uses an eight-speed dual-clutch, and the 296 Challenge Evo uses a seven-speed. Both cars share a dry weight of 2936 pounds because they omit the hybrid system’s 165-hp motor and 7.45-kWh battery.


Ferrari


Ferrari


Likewise, Ferrari simplified and stripped down the car’s exterior lines, but still baked extra performance into the clean looks. Thanks to a new fixed rear wing, belly pan, splitter, and vortex generators, the 296 Challenge Stradale generates 1357 pounds of downforce at 155 mph, 72% more than the 296 GTB. The Evo’s downforce was increased to over 1800 pounds at 155 mph. For higher top speeds on tracks with longer straights, Ferrari lets Challenge Evo drivers opt for a low-drag configuration that reduces minimum drag by 4%, offering a wider range of adjustment compared to its predecessor and broadening its operating window.

Ferrari


Ferrari

Ferrari


Ferrari already had a version of the 296 for its one-marque race series. The 296 Challenge offered from 2024-2026 kept the hybrid powertrain but still served as a major inspiration for the 296 Challenge Stradale, which inherited a lot of the track car’s heat management. In case you were thinking that the loss in power would handicap the cars on the track, fear not. Ferrari says that the lower weight and increased downforce helped the Challenge Evo shed 0.8 seconds per lap at the 5.245-km Mugello Circuit compared to its hybrid predecessor. The new car’s lower weight also helps tires last longer. That’s going to be important, as the Ferrari Challenge will begin a new format of three rounds featuring 40-minute endurance races starting at the second event of the season at Mugello Circuit.

With the V-8-powered 849 Testarossa and SF90 available only as hybrids, these new 296 variants are the purest mid-engine options available from Maranello. It doesn’t take a crystal ball to guess that these will be highly sought after. Ferrari hasn’t yet mentioned a price. They’ll be available late next year.
